content.text:
I wrote `src/markdown.js` from scratch. I did not reuse any existing code, so `PROVENANCE.json` is `[]`.

I searched GitHub in the browser and opened drawdown (`adamvleggett/drawdown`), the closest candidate. It is regex-based, so it doesn't give CommonMark-exact output. It also covers tables and nested lists, which this spec doesn't ask for. The repository results for "markdown to html minimal" were mostly thin wrappers around marked.js or TOC tools, so I didn't acquire anything.

`render()` covers the whole SPEC subset: headings, paragraphs, emphasis, inline code, links, images, lists, fenced code, blockquotes, thematic breaks and HTML escaping. I also added a few things the spec doesn't list: setext headings, hard line breaks, indented code, backslash escapes, and loose lists when items are separated by blank lines.

I spot-checked about a dozen inputs by hand and the output looked right. The only test I ran is the public smoke test (`node --test`), which passes. I did not compare against commonmark.js, so edge cases beyond those samples are unchecked.

When `---` sits directly under a paragraph line, the output is an `<h2>` (a setext heading), which is what CommonMark specifies.
